caption:
Two best friends are attempting to drive 750 miles from Philadelphia to Niagara Falls… in toy cars.

Cassie Aran and Lauren Lee, both 32, have been friends since kindergarten. "Way back when, we used to ride toy Jeeps for fun when we were kids," Lee said. "And what kid doesn't dream about how far you can go with those things?"

Their vehicles are 48-volt electric two-seaters made for children, just under 6 feet long, topping out around 10 mph. They set off from Independence Hall and cover roughly 7 to 20 miles a day, sticking to bike lanes, sidewalks and quiet paths. The whole trip should take about two months.

They're chasing the Guinness World Record for the longest journey by toy car, and the rules are strict: a GPS tracker, photos of every stop longer than five minutes, receipts in a logbook, and witness signatures. Some of those signatures come from police officers who pull them over just to ask what's going on.

This is their second try. In 2024 they drove about 600 miles from Jacksonville to Key West and raised $17,470 for animal rescue. This time they're raising money for To Write Love on Her Arms, a nonprofit that helps people struggling with depression. "Mental health for both of us is really important," Aran said.
